SUBJECT:  DIRECTOR AND LIBRARY MANAGER REPORT

BACKGROUND

At the request of the Library Board of Trustees, the Community Services Director and Library
Manager provide a monthly report to the Crowell Public Library Board of Trustees. The report
provides relevant administrative, operational, and financial updates, as well as information on
upcoming events, marketing and communication efforts, and customer feedback.

DISCUSSION

Personnel Update
The Library wrapped up the first round of interviews for the five part-time Library Assistant
positions open in Adult and Youth Services. Library Assistants provide support to Librarians by
working at the Reference Desk, assisting with collection management, and executing programs. Staff
plan to have second interviews before the end of the month and have new staff onboard by mid-
November.

Meet the Librarian Team - Tuesday, October 25 from 4 – 7 PM, Schow Patio
Staff are pleased to invite the community to submit their ideas regarding fresh, new library
programming! The team of Librarians is ready to gather input about the services and programs that
can support San Marino’s quality of life, as well as recreational and informational needs. Light
refreshments will be provided. Registration is not required. Hope to see you there!

Library A/C Status Update
Good news! The HVAC vendor moved the date for the compressor installation up to the week of
October 24. Parks and Public Works staff will lead a job walk-through with the vendor on October
24. Installation is planned for October 25 and may begin as early as 6 AM. On October 26, a portion
of the public parking lot will be closed for the crane. The job should conclude on October 27.

 San Marino Public Library Foundation (SMPLF) Update
  Literary Libations Recap
  The Foundation feels Literary Libations was a success and hope all in attendance enjoyed
  themselves. Alexander’s Prime Meats and Catering served excellent offerings to pair with
  the wide assortment of wine, beer, and spirit tastings. The evening included Council Member
  Steve Talt as the Paddle Raise emcee; Grace Chen, engraver and calligrapher, writing book
  plates on the spot; tasting tables for wines, local craft beers, spirits, and caviar.

  Over 180 people attended, 81 of the 86 silent auction offerings sold, and the event had 52
  sponsors. The Foundation is still in the midst of finalizing auction sales and feels assured they
  can provide support to fund a new ILS system and additional acquisitions. A portion of the
  net proceeds will also be allocated for the endowment fund the Foundation created with the
  Pasadena Community Foundation.

  – mid December
  - 2023 Open House – celebrating 90th anniversary of the Library in San Marino, 15th

Crain Art Gallery – New Exhibit
The current exhibit displays landscape paintings by the Plein Aires, a group of 20 artists working in
a variety of media. The reception for the Plein Aires was held on October 1, with 75 people in

exhibit is up through October 27.

Operational Staff Briefings
  Adult Programs
  Huntington Nurses Health Screening
  15 attendees in September and 12 in October received screenings for hypertension, heart
  disease, and diabetes from Huntington Hospital’s Nurses. These screenings provide the
  community with access to drop-in preventive services that support a healthy life and the
  Library is pleased to offer this free service to patrons.

  Huntington Nurses Flu Clinic
  55 attendees received their flu shot on September 28. This clinic provided the community
  with access to a free flu shot and peace of mind that they can protect themselves with flu
  season just around the corner.

  Chinese Club of San Marino
  On October 13, the Chinese Club provided a hands-on lesson on Chinese knotting. This fine
  art has its roots in antiquity and is believed to have evolved from folk art. 5 participants had
  the opportunity to make necklace using Chinese knotting techniques. This was the final
  lesson in the Chinese knotting series.

  Toastmasters Talk of the Town
  San Marino’s Toastmasters group had 12 people at their one meeting in September (the first
  one was cancelled due to A/C issues at the Library). 10 people attended the meetings in
  October. Participants were offered the opportunity to hone their presentation and speaking
  skills in a supportive and convenient setting.

  iPhone Beginner Class
  The iPhone class, which began meeting in September, continues with sessions throughout
  the month of October. The iPhone Beginner Class is a 6-week program that gives a crash
  course on the ways of the iPhone and is taught by community favorite, Edison Samuel.

   Participants are offered the opportunity to learn about the uses of their iPhone aside from
  just making phone calls.

  Youth Programs
  Family Storytime
  Three storytimes (105 in attendance) were offered during the month of September with
  individual themes of Chickens, Elephants, and Apples. Children used shakey egg musical
  instruments and sang and danced to the songs “I Know a Chicken” and “The Chicken Dance.”
  Music encourages children to express themselves through movement and play. Physical play
  stimulates the part of the brain that regulates emotions. Overall, music plays a vital role in
  the growth and development of early childhood learners.

  Author Visit with Jennifer Torres
  Due to A/C issues at the Library in early September, the Author Visit with children’s author,
  Jennifer Torres, has been rescheduled to March 2023. The program will be advertised in the
  Winter Community Services Guide. The first twenty children in attendance will receive a
  copy of Torres’ award-winning book, “Stef Soto, Taco Queen.”

  Passports
  Passport Services continue to be in high demand. In the month of September, 338 passports
  were processed, which resulted in $13,480 in revenue.

TO:  Chair and Trustees of the Library Board

FROM:  Cathi Johnson, Community Services Director

DATE:  October 24, 2022

SUBJECT:  REQUEST TO UPDATE AND RECOMMEND CITY COUNCIL TO
  CODIFY THE LIBRARY CODE OF CONDUCT

BACKGROUND

Patrons of the Crowell Public Library are subject to a Standards of Behavior policy (Attachment
1), last approved by the Library Board of Trustees on April 27, 2017. The vast majority of
incidents involving violations of the policy are handled by Library staff. Occasionally, however,
due to the severity of the incident or other potential safety concerns, the San Marino Police
Department (SMPD) is contacted for assistance. When a violation is severe enough to rise to the
level of a crime under the California Penal Code, the officers have clear authority to arrest or
remove an individual. However, when the violation of the policy does not rise to the level of a
crime under the Penal Code, the officers do not have similar authority to address the potential
safety concerns. This limitation creates frustration for Library staff, SMPD, and other library
patrons affected by the policy violation.

DISCUSSION

Attachment 2 is a revised Library Code of Conduct that is proposed to supersede the Standards
of Behavior and be codified into the San Marino Municipal Code. It is anticipated that the vast
majority of code of conduct issues would continue to be handled by Library staff, and would
usually just involve reminding patrons of the rules, or issuing warnings. In more extreme
circumstances, temporary suspension of library privileges or issuance of administrative citations
could be utilized.

In those rare instances where safety concerns are involved, codification would also allow for
more effective police intervention. The police would now be able to remove patrons or make
arrests for violations of the policy. These violations could then be prosecuted as either infractions
or misdemeanors by the City prosecutor. This should improve the library experience for all
patrons.

  Page 12 of 19
 RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the Board approve the updated Library Code of Conduct and request
that City Council approve and codify the policy into the San Marino Municipal Code.

ATTACHMENTS

  1. 2017 Standards of Behaviors
  2. Draft Library Code of Conduct

   STANDARDS OF BEHAVIOR
  April 2017

The Crowell Public Library is open to all members of the public. Patrons may remain in
the Library as long as necessary/appropriate to use the services, materials or facilities for
reading, studying, attending programs and obtaining information.

It is our goal to provide an atmosphere that is welcoming, comfortable, and consistent
with library purposes. The public is expected to behave in a manner that is respectful of
the library’s users and staff, materials and equipment, and facilities and premises. A
person who behaves otherwise will be required to leave the building.

General Guidelines
  1. The Crowell Public Library will uphold all state laws and local ordinances in
  regard to public behavior.

  2. The following activities are specifically prohibited:
  a. Damaging, mutilating, or illegally removing library materials or property.
  b. Violating the library’s Internet Use Policy.
  c. Eating or smoking in the building. Covered beverages (with lids or caps)
  are permitted.
  d. Smoking on library premises, including the outdoor patio.
  e. Bringing animals into the library except for service animals.
  f. Using restrooms for washing clothes or bathing.
  g. Parking bicycles in the library. Using skateboards, inline skates, etc. on
  library premises. (Ordinance number 977, 6-13-90; City Code 15.11.02)
  h. Entering staff areas.

  3. Patrons will respect the rights of other patrons and staff and not harass or annoy
  others by:
  a. Begging or soliciting.
  b. Engaging in loud, offensive or abusive language and/or gestures which are
  disturbing to others.
  c. Using personal radios, televisions, video games, cellular phones or other
  personal electronic devices which are disturbing to others.
  d. Creating a disturbance by yelling, running, throwing objects, misusing the
  facilities, or other disruptive behaviors.

  Page 14 of 19
  1
   4. Adults are responsible for the conduct of children in their care. Adults are
  responsible for monitoring the safety, activities and behavior of their children in
  the library.
  a. Library staff cannot care for children left unattended on the premises.
  b. Library staff cannot assume any parental responsibility for unattended
  children.
  c. Unattended children who violate the Library Standards of Behavior will be
  asked to telephone an adult (parent) for pick-up.
  d. Unattended children who are left on the premises after closing, or children
  who have been asked to leave the library because of Standards of Behavior
  violations and cannot reach their parent, will be turned over to the San
  Marino Police Department (Ordinance number O99-1129; City Code
  14.08.04)
  e. The children’s and young adult areas are intended to be used by children
  and adults accompanying children or those legitimately working with
  children’s materials.

  5. Patrons will maintain bodily hygiene as to not constitute a nuisance to other
  persons in the library.

  6. Patrons must be fully clothed at all times, including shirts and shoes.

  7. Patrons must be watchful of personal possessions. The library is not responsible
  for lost, damaged or stolen personal property.

Enforcement
  1. Violation of the foregoing may result in the patron’s library privilege being
  limited or revoked, removal of the patron from the building, or criminal
  prosecution if the conduct constitutes a violation of either State law or the San
  Marino Municipal Code.

  2. The City Librarian, upon staff recommendation, may revoke the patron’s library
  use privilege for a period up to one year.

  3. A library patron whose library privilege has been revoked may appeal the
  decision by submitting a completed Library Revocation Appeal form to the City
  Librarian within ten (10) days from the date of the determination letter.

  4. A patron whose library privilege has been revoked must schedule a meeting with
  the City Librarian prior to resumption of library privileges. The purpose of the
  meeting will be to review the Standards of Behavior policy.

Adopted by Library Board of Trustees April 27, 2017.

 Purpose. Section [XX] establishes a Code of Conduct expected of persons using the Crowell
Public Library and the processes to address violations of this Code of Conduct. The purposes for
the Code of Conduct are to ensure that all persons have the ability to use library services and
resources, to ensure that library staff may efficiently provide library services and resources, to
prevent disruption to such library services and resources, and to further a peaceful, quiet, and
orderly environment in which to learn.

  1. Definitions.
For the purpose of this section, the following definitions shall apply unless the context clearly
indicates or requires a different meaning.
  (1) CHILDREN’S AREA. The area of the library specifically designated as such by the
  library to provide library services and resources that meets the needs of young
  library users.
  (2) CODE. The San Marino Municipal Code.
  (3) CRIME. The same definition as in Cal. Penal Code § 15. A violation of § [XX] is a
  misdemeanor crime under Cal. Gov’t Code § 36900.
  (4) ENFORCEMENT OFFICER. The City Manager, or the City Manager’s designee.
  The City Manager’s designees include, without limitation: the Community Services
  Director and Library Services Manager, the Police Chief and police officers, and
  the city’s Code Enforcement Supervisor and code enforcement officers.
  (5) LIBRARY. The Crowell Public Library, including but not limited to its collection
  areas, meeting rooms, and stores.
  (6) LIBRARY PREMISES. The library, and library grounds and parking facilities to the
  extent that the grounds or parking facilities are owned, controlled, or maintained
  by the city.
  (7) LIBRARY PRIVILEGES. The privilege of entering onto library premises and utilizing
  any services or resources of the Crowell Public Library.
  (8) SERVICE ANIMAL. A dog that has been individually trained to do work or
  perform tasks for an individual with a disability, as defined under the Americans
  with Disabilities Act.
  (9) SHOE. An item worn on the human foot with a sole.
  (10) SMOKE or SMOKING. The same definition contained in Business and Professions
  Code § 22950.5(c), and includes vaping.
  (11) WHEELED CONVEYANCES. Any wheeled device used for conveyance or
  transportation, including bicycles, skates, skateboards, collapsible scooters,
  wheelies, and hover boards. This does not include medically required equipment,
  or wheelchairs or strollers carrying people who cannot use the library facilities
  without the assistance of such devices.

  2. Criminal conduct. A person may not commit or attempt to commit any crime punishable
  under state or federal law or this code on library premises, including, but not limited to:
  (1) Assault or battery, as defined in Cal. Penal Code §§ 240 and 242.
  (2) Theft, as defined in Cal. Penal Code § 484.
  (3) Obstructing or intimidating business operators, public agencies or customers, as
  defined in Cal. Penal Code § 602.1.
  (4) Vandalism, as defined in Cal. Penal Code § 594.

  Page 16 of 19
   (5) Indecent exposure or lewd or obscene conduct, as defined in Cal. Penal Code §
  314
  (6) Possession of designated controlled substances, as defined in Cal. Health and
  Safety Code §§ 11350 and 11351.
  (7) Disorderly conduct, as defined in Cal. Penal Code § 647.
  (8) Trespass, as defined in Cal. Penal Code §§ 602 and 634.
  (9) Smoking, vaping or using tobacco products, as defined in Business and Professions
  Code § 22950.5(c).
  (10) Curfew violations, as defined in Chapter [XX] of this code.
  (11) Consumption of alcohol in a public place, as defined in Chapter [XX] of this code.

3. Rules of conduct. The following behaviors are disruptive and do not further a peaceful,
  quiet, and orderly environment to learn. In addition to the criminal conduct listed in §
  [XX]), no person may engage in any of the following activities or behaviors while on library
  premises:
  (1) Loud or disruptive behavior, including yelling, talking loudly, running, throwing
  objects, abusive or threatening language, or other behavior which disturbs the
  quiet environment of the library.
  (2) Using profane, obscene, imminently threatening, or violent language toward
  library staff or other persons.
  (3) Harassing or the making of unwanted verbal or physical advances toward library
  staff or persons on library premises.
  (4) Possessing any unlawful or illegal substance on library premises.
  (5) Using personal equipment in the library (such as cellular phones and audio players)
  in a manner that is disruptive, noisy, or unsafe. Personal equipment or electronic
  devices must be muted and made inaudible to other persons while in the library.
  Cell phones must be set to mute or vibrate.
  (6) Possessing any beverage in the library without a spill-proof lid.
  (7) Consuming any food or beverages in a non-designated location within the library.
  (8) Bringing, possessing, or maintaining on the library premises any garbage or item
  that emits a foul odor that disturbs other library users or staff.
  (9) Bringing or using any shopping carts or other wheeled conveyances within the
  library, on entryways or walkways, in a manner that blocks any passageway on
  library premises.
  (10) Smoking, vaping, or using of any tobacco products in the library or within 20 feet
  of entrances to the library.
  (11) Consuming or possessing alcoholic beverages on library premises, unless
  otherwise approved by the city as part of a special event.
  (12) Leaving backpacks, suitcases, or other large items unattended in the library (other
  than leaving them at a study carrel while researching the collection for materials),
  or keeping those items with one in a manner that obstructs entrances, exits, aisles
  or passageways, or otherwise impedes access to library resources and services.
  (13) Bringing animals, other than service animals there solely to assist a person with
  disabilities with tasks directly related to that person’s disability, into the library,
  including but not limited to collection areas, meeting rooms, and stores.

  Page 17 of 19
   (14) Using library facilities for the purpose of sleeping, bathing, shaving, washing clothes
  or other similar activities.
  (15) Entering the library or remaining in the library, including, but not limited to,
  collection areas, meeting rooms, and stores, without wearing shoes or clothes
  that cover the upper and lower torso area.
  (16) Soliciting, panhandling, selling products without written authorization from library
  staff, or otherwise conducting business (including tutoring for a fee) within the
  library.
  (17) By a person 18 years of age or older, and in the absence of accompanying children
  or the permission of library staff, using or occupying of the children’s areas of the
  library; these areas are specifically designed to meet the needs of young library
  users and must remain open to those users and the adults accompanying them.
  (18) Moving library equipment or furniture without library staff knowledge or
  permission.
  (19) Tampering with library equipment such as computers, rental equipment,
  photocopy machines, elevators.
  (20) Carrying or possessing on library premises weapons such as guns, chains, clubs,
  and knives.
  (21) Making unauthorized entry into any “staff only” area in the library premises.
  (22) Refusing to relinquish computer equipment or other library resources after
  scheduled time period for use has expired.
  (23) Causing overcrowding in library seating areas by sitting more than four persons
  to a table, two persons to a computer workstation, or one person to a carrel or
  chair.
  (24) Failing to leave the library at closing time.
  (25) Destroying, defacing or illegally removing library materials or property, including,
  but not limited to writing in, highlighting or annotating library materials; cutting,
  tearing or removing pages and parts of pages from library materials.
  (26) Using library internet and computers in violation of any posted restrictions or on
  screen notices; including, but not limited to misusing, altering or tampering with
  computer hardware or software; use of other patrons’ library cards/accounts for
  internet access, disabling firewall or accessing blocked sites.
  (27) Entering and bringing an excessive amount of personal items or baggage into the
  library or place it in a manner where it restricts the usage of the library by other
  patrons and constitutes a nuisance. Personal items may not take up a footprint
  that exceeds three and a half by three and a half feet.
  (28) Parking bicycles in the library. Using skateboards, inline skates, etc. on library
  premises.

4. Supervision of minors.
  (1) No person under the age of nine years of age may enter, use, or remain on library
  premises without being accompanied by a person 18 years of age or older.
  (2) Any person 18 years of age or older, who brings a child under the age of nine
  years of age into the library, must supervise and accompany that child at all times.
  (3) Unattended children who are left on the premises after closing, or children who
  have been asked to leave the library because of Standards of Behavior violations

  Page 18 of 19
   and cannot reach their parent, will be turned over to the San Marino Police
  Department

5. Enforcement.
  (1) Any enforcement officer may enforce against any violation of the rules of conduct
  contained in §[XX].
  (2) A violation of § [XX]is punishable as an infraction or misdemeanor as set forth in
  section 1.04.02.
  (3) In the alternative, an enforcement officer may enforce against any violation of §
  [XX]by issuing notices of violation or administrative citations. The enforcement
  officer may issue a notice of violation or an administrative citation to a person in
  violation of the rules of conduct in accordance with Chapter 1.06 of this code.
  The enforcement officer may order the removal of any person from the library
  for any violation of the rules of conduct concurrently with the issuance of an
  administrative citation. Any person removed pursuant to such an order may not
  re-enter onto library premises for the remainder of the business day. Any person
  who re-enters the library premises after such removal will be considered a
  trespasser.

6. Suspension of library privileges.
  In addition to any other punishment provided for at law, any person who commits or
  attempts to commit a crime or violates one or more of the rules of conduct set forth in
  this § [XX] while on library premises may have their library privileges suspended. A person
  whose library privileges have been suspended may not enter onto library premises or use
  the services of the Crowell Public Library during the term of their suspension. A written
  notice of suspension of library privileges will be issued to the person. The following
  schedule governs the length of a suspension of library privileges:
  (1) For a person’s first violation, library privileges will be suspended for one week.
  (2) For a person’s second violation within a 12-month period, library privileges will
  be suspended for four weeks.
  (3) For a person’s third violation within a 12-month period, library privileges will be
  suspended for 16 weeks.
  (4) If a person commits four or more violations within a 12-month period, library
  privileges will be suspended for 12 months.

7. Fines.
  The City Council may set by resolution the fines to be assessed for violations of the rules
  of conduct. If no amount is specified by resolution of the City Council, the fines set forth
  in § [XX] of this code may apply.

8. Appeals.
  A person may appeal an administrative citation or suspension of library privilege in
  accordance with the administrative hearing procedures outlined in Chapter [XX] of this
  code.

  Page 19 of 19

MINUTES
  REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE SAN MARINO LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES
  MONDAY, OCTOBER 24, 2022 AT 8:00 A.M.
  BARTH ROOM
  CROWELL PUBLIC LIBRARY

CALL TO ORDER: Chairperson Domier called the regular meeting to order at 8:01 a.m. via
teleconference.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Chairperson Domier led the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL:  PRESENT: Alternate Wahl (arrived at 8:04 a.m.), Trustee Osegueda, Trustee
  Derry, Trustee Chien, Vice Chairperson Sadun, and Chairperson Domier

  ABSENT: Alternate Wu

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The following person(s) provided comment:
  - None

BOARD OF TRUSTEES REPORTS

1. CHAIRPERSON REPORT

Chairperson Domier shared how wonderful his experiences have been at Family Storytime and how
much he enjoyed Literary Libations. He added that despite the new formal approach to the advisory
body meetings, the goal is to make them more transparent and accessible to the community.

2. TRUSTEE REPORTS

Vice Chairperson Sadun inquired if the Library plans to offer Narcan and train employees on how
to administer it like the Los Angeles County libraries. Library Manager Vera responded that there
have been no requests for that service. Director Johnson added that she will run the idea past Fire
Chief Rueda, who oversees emergency management. Vice Chairperson Sadun also shared about her
recent visit to Spain in which she visited the Valencia Library.

Trustee Chien, Trustee Derry, Trustee Osegueda, and Alternate Wahl did not have anything to
report at this time.

3. CRAIN ART GALLERY LIAISON REPORT

Vice Chairperson Sadun shared the Plein Aires reception was well attended, and the display will be
followed by artwork by Linda Mollno with a reception on December 3. In addition, she shared that
the Committee booked five artists for the February through March display.
 LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES MINUTES  REGULAR MEETING
OCTOBER 24, 2022  PAGE 2 OF 3

4. SAN MARINO CENTER RENOVATION UPDATE REPORT

Chairperson Domier shared that construction is well underway on the San Marino Center, with
estimated completion in August or September 2023. Director Johnson shared her goal to have the
San Marino Center renamed to the San Marino Community Center. She explained that the name
change will be run by the Council Liaisons and potentially the entire City Council.

5. FRIENDS OF THE CROWELL PUBLIC LIBRARY LIAISON REPORT
Trustee Derry did not have anything to report at this time.

6. SAN MARINO PUBLIC LIBRARY FOUNDATION LIAISON REPORT
Trustee Chien shared about the success of the Literary Libations event and details about the
upcoming Bookmark Contest and Open House.

NEW BUSINESS

7. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

The following person(s) provided comment:
  - None

Trustee Derry moved, seconded by Vice Chairperson Sadun, to approve the minutes from
September 26, 2022.

Motion passed by the following vote:

AYES:  Trustee Osegueda, Trustee Derry, Trustee Chien, Vice Chairperson Sadun,
  Chairperson Domier
NOES:  None
ABSTAIN:  None
ABSENT:  None

8. DIRECTOR AND LIBRARY MANAGER REPORT

Director Johnson and Library Manager Vera presented the staff report.

The following person(s) provided comment:
  - None

9. REQUEST TO UPDATE AND RECOMMEND CITY COUNCIL TO CODIFY THE
  LIBRARY CODE OF CONDUCT

Director Johnson presented the staff report.
 LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES MINUTES  REGULAR MEETING
OCTOBER 24, 2022  PAGE 3 OF 3

Trustee Derry inquired about the issue of unhoused individuals sleeping on premises. Director
Johnson shared that there are signs posted around the facility that speak to no trespassing and the
Police Department has been assisting with this issue. Chairperson Dornier inquired about the fines
listed on page 19. Director Johnson responded that the "[XX]" are placeholders that reference
sections in the Municipal Code and will be filled in when the item goes before the City Council.
Trustee Osegueda inquired if staff have been trained on what to do when patrons enter the facility
with excessive personal belongings. Director Johnson responded that this issue is addressed in
Section 3, Item 27. Vice Chairperson Sadun suggested that the Code of Conduct be posted in the
Library to allow staff to refer to it when handling conduct issues. Director Johnson responded that
the Code will reside on the website and on over-sized poster, flyers, etc.; it will be reviewed with
staff on an annual basis and during onboarding. Trustee Chien inquired about the status of the
surveillance cameras at the Library. Library Manager Vera responded that the Library utilizes Nest
cameras, but staff have only been able to access a live stream and are unable to save any recordings.
Director Johnson added that a new camera system was requested in the budget cycle and is on
staffs' radar. Trustee Osegueda requested that the word "safety" be added to the title of the policy.

The following person(s) provided comment:
  None

Vice Chairperson Sadun moved, seconded by Trustee Osegueda, to approve the updated the Library
Code of Conduct and request that City Council approve and codify the policy into the San Marino
Municipal Code.

Motion passed by the following vote:

AYES:  Trustee Osegueda, Trustee Derry, Trustee Chien, Vice Chairperson Sadun,
  Chairperson Dornier
NOES:  None
ABSTAIN:  None
ABSENT:  None
